newsitem.title: USA: CME feeder cattle post sharp closing gains on cash.
newsitem.headline: CME feeder cattle post sharp closing gains on cash.

text.p: Reports of higher cash feeder cattle prices helped lift CME feeder cattle futures for sharp closing gains after April posted a new high. Live cattle also rose on ideas of stabilizing cash cattle prices, traders said.
Feeder cattle ended up 1.125 to 0.700 cent a lb with May up most at 72.025 cents. April posted a new high of 72.300 cents. Live cattle closed 0.175 to 0.600 higher with June up 0.275 at 64.750 cents.
Feeder cattle rose from the start, boosted by a higher CME feeder cattle index and expectations of further gains in the index over the next couple of days, traders said.

Interest for replacement feeders has been fairly good and easing feed costs overall added to stronger cash market ideas. Large death losses in the Dakotas after harsh winter weather and a recent blizzard and ensuing flooding, will also make for tighter feeder supplies later, some sources noted.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.37 at $70.85 per cwt and was seen rising soon to $72.00.
Dan Vaught, livestock analyst with AG Edwards, cited a number of factors for demand in feeders.
Recent stronger fed cattle prices have sparked demand for replacement feeders, sources said.
Also, feeder cattle supplies are tightening based on previous projections and increased heifer retention, Vaught said.

USDA reported feeder cattle at the key Oklahoma City auction Monday sold at prices steady to $1.00 higher than last week's sales, with steers weighing 700 to 799 lbs selling at $71.50 to $75.50 per cwt this week.

"With all the bullishness in here and the higher calf and cow prices, everybody is wanting to catch this next up in the cycle in the cattle market, so I think heifer retention is way up and this is cutting down on the potential feeder supply for the second half of the year," Vaught said.
Long term impact from calf losses this winter and spring is also bullish to deferred feeder contracts, he added.

FIMAT Futures USA, Refco and Dean Witter bought May late. Cargill Investor Services bought early while also spreading long October live cattle/short May feeders. ADM Investor Services sold early, pit sources said.

Lack of a bearish report and the discount futures hold to cash cattle prices supported live cattle futures. Although initial reaction to Friday's USDA cattle report was neutral, analysts and traders noted that the March marketing figure showed feedlots were current going into April and placements onto feedlots were less than had been feared.

Friday's data showed April 1 on-feed supplies at feedlots with 1,000 head or more capacity in the seven key states at 107 percent of a year ago versus the average of analysts' estimates at 107.6 percent. Marketings during March were 101 percent of a year ago versus the average estimate of 100.6. Placements were 102 percent of a year ago compared with 103.3 estimated.

Expectations cash cattle will hold a steady to firm tone going into May added to support. Packers will need cattle to fill beef needs during one of the best demand periods of the year that lies ahead. That period includes Memorial Day in May and Fathers Day in June. Outdoor grilling moves into full gear during May in many areas, traders added.

Iowa Grain, R.J. O'Brien and Prudential Securities bought April while Refco bought June. In cattle options, commercials bought and sold October 70 calls. Volatility in June was weak on out of the money put selling, pit sources said.
